we prove the local-in-time existence, uniqueness and stability of solutions for the barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes system, with initial density in $\mathcal{D}^{'}$, and initial data in $\mathcal D^{'}$ for the velocity, in the case when the initial density is bounded away from zero, and the pressure is a smooth and increasing function of the density.
we have shown that the barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes system is well-posed in critical Besov spaces for large initial data, without assuming smallness on $\rho-\bar{\rho}$.

we can obtain a unique global solution for the barotropic viscous compressible fluid system with large initial data having critical Besove regularity.
we can prove the well-posedness of the compressible viscous barotropic fluid system in the critical space with large initial data.

we prove that the Cauchy problem for barotropic compressible viscous fluid flow is locally well posed in the space $L^{p}(\RR^N)\times B^{\NN}_{q,r}(\RR^ N)$, where $p$ and $q$ are two positive real numbers such that $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{N}{q} < \frac{N+1}{2}$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have obtained a priori estimates in Besov spaces with a gain of one derivative for the velocity, and a gain of two derivatives for the density.
the density can be more regular than the velocity.
